subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source gap is high-confidence, but fallback behavior changes permission-sensitive session, provider/model, and compatibility semantics that repository policy treats as maintainer-owned product direction.

options.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and add clearer docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair Replacement PR First
options.body: Use the linked fork PR as source material only after conflicts, phantom-agent guards, diagnostics, and real Discord proof are addressed.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, tests, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the shared resolver, Discord route helper, docs, and default-account routing decisions.
